public.title: The Opened Insect Nests
public.incident: Several social-insect nests have been opened overnight, but the survey records little blood, fur, or prolonged digging at any one site.
public.atmosphere: The visits are quiet, selective, and repeated beneath forest cover.
public.question: Which species made these feeding marks, and what best explains the narrow target?

explanationChoices.label: Specialist foraging
explanationChoices.description: A nocturnal feeder is opening nests to collect ants or termites.

explanationChoices.label: Generalist digging
explanationChoices.description: A soil forager encountered the colonies while searching for varied prey.

explanationChoices.label: Colony disease
explanationChoices.description: The insects abandoned damaged nests before any vertebrate arrived.

explanationChoices.label: Human disturbance
explanationChoices.description: People opened the nests and an animal was blamed because it was nearby.

explanationFeedback.specialist-foraging: The focused openings and repeated nocturnal visits fit a narrow social-insect diet.
explanationFeedback.generalist-digging: The evidence clusters at organized colonies rather than showing a broad search through soil.
explanationFeedback.nest-disease: Disease might empty a colony, but it does not explain the external opening marks and recurring visits.
explanationFeedback.human-disturbance: No tool pattern or daytime access record supports human opening at the sampled nests.

resolution.headline: A precise insect specialist
resolution.diagnosis: Sunda pangolin feeding opened the nests. Strong claws expose chambers and a long sticky tongue collects ants and termites.
evidenceChain: The target is an organized insect colony rather than general soil prey.
The visitor moves alone and under cover at night.
Limb and diet evidence support climbing, digging, and concentrated insect feeding.
resolution.ecologicalRole: By disturbing nests and consuming social insects, specialized myrmecophages connect forest soils, insect colonies, and vertebrate predation.
resolution.taxonomy: Manis javanica belongs to Pholidota, a distinct mammal order more closely related to carnivorans than to armadillos.
resolution.misconception: Protective scales do not make pangolins reptiles; they are placental mammals.
rejectedAlternatives: A generalist soil hunter would leave a broader search pattern.
Colony disease does not account for the repeated external opening marks.
